documentation.title: Confirm On Delete
documentation.standard:
Commands that delete or irreversibly change data must ask WP_CLI::confirm() first. A command is destructive when its name (the @subcommand, the registered name, or the method name) contains a whole word such as delete, remove, flush, truncate, reset, purge, destroy, drop, clear, wipe, uninstall or erase, or when it calls a content-destroying API (wp_delete_post(), $wpdb->delete(), a $wpdb->query() with DELETE/TRUNCATE/DROP, ...). Same-class helpers are followed; declare a confirmation in another class with "@cli-standards confirm-delegated <reason>".
Requirement: E1 (MUST, error). Error codes: MissingConfirm. Properties: destructiveFunctions (APIs that make a command destructive; '->name' means a $wpdb method), ignoreMethods, ignoreClasses.
